name: Villa Savoye
tagline: House by Le Corbusier in Poissy, France.

construction.quote: It was designed by the Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier and his cousin Pierre Jeanneret with interior and furnishing by Charlotte Perriand, and built between 1928 and 1931 using reinforced concrete.

scenes.title: Background
scenes.caption: Pierre and Eugénie Savoye approached Le Corbusier about building a country home in Poissy in the spring of 1928.
scenes.quote: Pierre and Eugénie Savoye approached Le Corbusier about building a country home in Poissy in the spring of 1928.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: After being purchased by the neighbouring school, it became the property of the French state in 1958.
scenes.quote: After being purchased by the neighbouring school, it became the property of the French state in 1958.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: After surviving several proposals to demolish it, it was designated as an official French historical monument in 1965 (a rare event, as Le Corbusier was still alive).
scenes.quote: After surviving several proposals to demolish it, it was designated as an official French historical monument in 1965 (a rare event, as Le Corbusier was still alive).

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: It was thoroughly renovated between 1985 and 1997, and the refurbished house is now open to visitors year round under the care of the Centre des monuments nationaux.
scenes.quote: It was thoroughly renovated between 1985 and 1997, and the refurbished house is now open to visitors year round under the care of the Centre des monuments nationaux.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: In July 2016, the house and 16 other buildings by Le Corbusier, spread over seven countries, were inscribed as The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier World Heritage Site by UNESCO.
